syllabus_metadata.title: Mathematics Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education Form I-IV
syllabus_metadata.subject: Mathematics

competences.specific_competence: 1.1 Use numerical skills in different contexts

learning_activities.activity: (a) Explain the basic concepts of Mathematics (Meaning of mathematics, branches of mathematics, relationship between mathematics and other subjects, importance of mathematics)
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Guide students to discuss meaning of mathematics and branches of mathematics
Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on importance of mathematics in daily life
Jigsaw: Guide students to explain the relationship of mathematics with other disciplines
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The basic concept of mathematics are clearly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Charts of relationships between mathematics and other fields, real life objects, Math Games and Apps, Educational channels

learning_activities.activity: (b) Explain the concept of rational, irrational, and real numbers
teaching_learning_methods: Observation: Provide students with visual aids like bars/strips or circles and guide them to cut the aids in small equal parts. Relate their responses to the meaning of fractions

Problem solving: Organise students in manageable groups and assign each group word problems that require students to apply their knowledge of fractions, decimals and percentages to real word scenarios. Guide them to present the results and relate their findings with rational numbers
Exploration: Guide students to relate real numbers to real-life situations, for example, money and measurement
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Rational, irrational, and real numbers are well explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Calculator, Charts of real numbers, ruler, tape measure, graph papers, number line chart

learning_activities.activity: (c) Convert repeating/recurring decimals into fractions and vice versa; Represent rational numbers on a number line
teaching_learning_methods: Problem solving: Provide students with examples of decimals and guide them to identify repeating/recurring decimals, and convert repeating/recurring decimals into fractions and vice versa and share with the rest of the class through presentations

Group discussion: Organise students in manageable groups to draw number lines. Guide them to discuss steps of representing rational numbers on a number line and share their results with the rest of the class through presentations
Problem solving: Guide students to suggest real-life problems involving rational numbers. Ask them to locate points on the number line and perform calculations based on the given scenario
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Repeating/recurring decimals are correctly converted into fractions; Rational numbers are well represented on the number line
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Calculator, Charts of real numbers, ruler, tape measure, graph papers

learning_activities.activity: (d) Explain the concept of inequalities and absolute values of real numbers
teaching_learning_methods: Intuitive approach: Guide students visual aids such as number line charts and graphing tools to explore the basic concepts of inequalities and absolute values of real numbers
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Absolute values and inequalities in real numbers are properly determined

competences.specific_competence: 1.2 Use ratios and proportions in daily life

learning_activities.activity: (a) Describe the importance of numbers in real-life situations; Explain the concept of ratios and proportions
teaching_learning_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the students to describe the importance of numbers and apply numbers in real-life situations

Group discussion: Organise students in manageable groups to discuss and come up with real-life scenarios involving the concept of ratios and proportions. Share with the rest of the class through presentations
Jigsaw: Guide students to explore how other subjects relate to concept of ratios and proportions
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Importance of numbers are well described; Ratios and proportions are clearly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Money, charts of real-life scenarios, interest calculators, and games, real objects, and bank statements

teaching_learning_methods: Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students to solve ratio and proportion problems and share the results with classmates
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Problems on ratios and proportions are correctly solved
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Calculator, Charts of real numbers, ruler, tape measure, graph papers, number line chart

competences.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts in geometry and algebra
competences.specific_competence: 2.1 Use geometry, approximations, relations and functions in various contexts

learning_activities.activity: (a) Explain the concept of approximations (rounding off, significant figures, and decimal places)
teaching_learning_methods: Brainstorming: In manageable groups guide Students to explore the concept of approximations and share their findings with other groups
Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students to pair up to discuss their ideas, thereafter, some of the pairs share their ideas with the whole class
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Charts of a number line, estimation jars, estimation games and applications

learning_activities.activity: (b) Round off numbers and estimate values of expressions; (c) Approximate numbers to the required significant figures and decimal places
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: In manageable groups, guide students to round off numbers and estimate values of expressions and share their findings
Jigsaw: Guide students to use real-life examples to approximate numbers to the required significant figures and decimal places
Problem solving: Assess the accuracy of answers provided by students when approximating numbers and provide them with feedback
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Numbers are rounded off and values of expressions are correctly estimated; Numbers are approximated to required significant figures and decimal places correctly
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Charts of a number line, estimation jars, estimation games and applications

learning_activities.activity: (d) Use approximations in computations and measurements of quantities in various contexts
teaching_learning_methods: Jigsaw: Organise students in manageable groups to discover the use of approximations in computations and measurements of quantities in various contexts
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Approximations are correctly applied in computations and measurements
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Beam balance, mathematical software such as MATLAB, and GeoGebra, real objects

competences.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts in geometry and algebra
competences.specific_competence: 2.2 Use algebra and matrices in problem solving

learning_activities.activity: (a) Explore the basic tenets of algebra (algebraic expressions and equations, linear simultaneous equations of two unknowns, inequalities in one unknown)
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Organize students in manageable groups, guide them to discuss algebraic expressions and equations
Visual representations: Provide learners with visual aids such as diagrams, charts, and graphs to illustrate the graphs of linear equations
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of algebra are correctly explored
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Beam balance, mathematical software such as MATLAB, and GeoGebra, real objects, Algebra animations

learning_activities.activity: (b) Use algebraic expressions to model situations (word problems into algebraic expressions and equations)
teaching_learning_methods: Problem solving: Incorporate word problems that require students to translate verbal descriptions into algebraic expressions and equations. Guide them to identify key words that indicate mathematical operations
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Algebraic expressions are applied to model situations correctly
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Beam balance, mathematical software such as MATLAB, and GeoGebra, real objects, Algebra animations

learning_activities.activity: (c) Solve simultaneous linear equations using substitution and elimination methods; Solve inequalities in one unknown
teaching_learning_methods: Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students in pair to solve simultaneous equations using substitution and elimination methods. Thereafter, allow some of the pairs to share their results with the whole class
Group discussion: In manageable groups, guide the students to solve inequalities in one unknown and present results for common understanding
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simultaneous linear equations are solved correctly; Inequalities are solved properly
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Number line chart, graphing calculator, real objects

competences.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts in coordinate geometry, trigonometry, circles, vectors, probability and statistics
competences.specific_competence: 3.1 Use basic coordinate geometry, trigonometry and vectors skills in daily life

learning_activities.activity: (a) Explore the basic tenets of coordinate geometry (gradient and equations of a straight line, graphs of linear equations)
teaching_learning_methods: Collaborative learning: Guide students to use visual aids, such as graphs and coordinate planes to establish the relationship between coordinates and geometrical shapes
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Basic tenets of coordinate geometry are explored
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Mathematical software such as MATLAB, and GeoGebra, Maple, Mathematica, graph papers

learning_activities.activity: (b) Find the gradient/ slope of a line
teaching_learning_methods: Problem solving: In manageable groups, guide the students to determine the slope of a given line
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Gradient of line is found properly

learning_activities.activity: (c) Determine the equation of a straight line and draw its graph
teaching_learning_methods: Visual representation: Utilize visual aids like diagrams and charts to illustrate the concept of a straight line visually. Provide examples of different types of straight lines and their corresponding equations and draw their graphs
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Equation of straight line is determined and its graph is properly drawn

teaching_learning_methods: Visual representation: Guide students to use visual aids such as a coordinate plane, graph paper, or interactive whiteboard to plot points, draw lines, and interpret the graph
Group discussion: In manageable groups, guide the students to solve linear simultaneous equations graphically
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simultaneous equations are correctly solved graphically

learning_activities.activity: (e) Use mathematical software to solve and draw graphs of simultaneous equations
teaching_learning_methods: Use of technology: Guide students to use mathematical software such as Excel, GeoGebra, Mathematica, MATLAB to solve and draw graphs of simultaneous equations
Problem solving: In manageable groups, provide students with plenty examples and exercise to solve and draw graphs of simultaneous equations using mathematical software
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simultaneous equations are solved and drawn correctly
